content.overview: BNS s. 48 — Abetment outside India for offence in India.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
New. Abetment outside India of an offence committed in India is now expressly covered — closing a territorial gap the IPC left open. A BNS provision with no single IPC predecessor. Treat it as a fresh offence.
In student language: BNS s. 48 is the rule on “Abetment outside India for offence in India”. The section provides that a person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, without and beyond India, abets the commission of any act in India which would constitute an offence if committed in India. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 48 exists so that “Abetment outside India for offence in India” has a closed legal test in Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: The inchoate trio. Abetment now covers extra-territorial aid; conspiracy and attempt sit next to it.

The provision in detail
48. A person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, without and beyond India, abets the commission of any act in India which would constitute an offence if committed in India

Essential ingredients
1. A person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, without and beyond India, abets the commission of any act in India which would constitute an offence if committed in India

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, in country X, instigates B, to commit a murder in India, A is guilty of abetting murder

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 48 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 48 (Abetment outside India for offence in India) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 48 (Abetment outside India for offence in India), Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) A person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, without and beyond India, abets the commission of any act in India which would constitute an offence if committed in India
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 48 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 48 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
